column2: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under plenty of water, rubbing for 1–2 minutes; this removes the bitter taste.
Bring the quinoa to the boil with the water; cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Spread out in a wide dish and cool completely.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes small; chop the parsley finely.
Dice the carrot, courgette and pepper small.
Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the carrot first for 2 minutes, then add the courgette and pepper and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add the water and a little salt and bring to the boil.
Remove from the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Pick over the buckwheat, wash and drain.
Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the onion for 3 minutes, then the carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the buckwheat and toast for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the hot water and a little salt; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 15–20 minutes until the grains are soft and the water absorbed.
Remove from the heat and rest for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Cook the couscous in salted boiling water for the packet time and drain.
Chop the pepper small; drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the pepper for 5 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and heat for 3 minutes; season with salt.
Add the couscous and toss for 1 minute.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve hot.
Cook the milk and oats in a small pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
If it thickens, add 2–3 spoonfuls of hot milk.
Peel and dice the apples; mix with cinnamon and spread in the ovenproof dish.
Take the butter cold from the fridge and cut into small cubes.
Rub the oats, flour and butter with your fingertips into coarse crumbs.
Scatter the crumbs evenly over the apples; don't press down.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the apples are soft and the top golden.
Remove from the oven and cool for 10 minutes; the fruit juices are very hot.
Prick the aubergines in several places with a fork; char over a gas flame or in a 220°C oven for 25–30 minutes until the skins blacken and the insides are completely soft.
When cool enough, peel and finely chop the flesh with a knife; drain off the bitter juice.
Whisk the yoghurt with crushed garlic and a little salt until smooth.
Add the aubergine to the yoghurt and mix.
It keeps in a covered container in the fridge for 2 days.
Preheat the oven to 200°C; line two trays with baking paper.
Peel the aubergines in stripes and dice; soak in salted water for 15 minutes, then squeeze and pat dry.
Dice the courgettes and potatoes.
Toss each vegetable separately with oil and spread on the trays; potatoes need 30–35 minutes, courgette and aubergine 20–25 minutes.
Heat the remaining oil in a pan and stir the garlic for 30 seconds; add the tomato and a little salt and cook for 10 minutes until saucy.
Mix the vegetables on a serving plate.
Pour the tomato sauce over the top; serve warm or cold.
Cut the chicken into large cubes.
Mix the yoghurt, curry powder, oil and a little salt.
Coat the chicken in the sauce and leave covered in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; cut the pepper into strips.
Spread the chicken and peppers in a single layer in the ovenproof dish.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway.
Preheat the oven to 175°C; grease and flour the tin or line it with baking paper.
The eggs and sugar should be at room temperature; whisk with a mixer for 4–5 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Add the milk, oil and orange zest and whisk for 30 seconds more.
Sift the flour with the baking powder and fold in with a spatula from bottom to top; overmixing makes the cake tough.
Pour the batter into the tin.
Bake for about 35 minutes.
Don't open the oven door for the first 25 minutes or the cake will sink.
Insert a toothpick in the centre: if it comes out dry, it is cooked.
Leave in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack; slice once completely cool.
Bring the quinoa to the boil with twice its volume of water; cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the grains open and the water is absorbed.
Dice the cucumber and pepper small.
Dice the avocado just before serving and toss with lemon juice so it doesn't brown.
Combine the cooled quinoa with the vegetables.
Char the peppers over a gas flame or in the oven for 10–15 minutes until the skins blacken.
Leave them to sweat in a covered container for 10 minutes, then peel; remove the seeds.
Chop the peppers small and drain off the juice.
Add the peppers to the yoghurt and mix.
Dice the courgette and carrot small.
Combine the drained couscous with the vegetables and toss for 1 minute.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease the muffin tin.
Dice the pepper and courgette small; squeeze the courgette lightly.
Beat the eggs; add the vegetables and crumbled cheese and mix.
Fill the moulds three-quarters full; they rise as they bake.
Leave in the tin for 5 minutes, then turn out.
Cut the chicken into thin strips.
Cut the carrot and pepper into thin strips.
Cook the noodles for the packet time and drain; rinse briefly in cold water so they don't stick.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and stir-fry the chicken over high heat for 6–7 minutes.
Add the vegetables and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, keeping them crisp.
Add the noodles and soy sauce and toss for 1 minute; soy sauce is salty, so don't add salt.
Peel and dice the apples small; toss with 1 spoon of flour so they don't sink.
Add the milk and oil and whisk for 30 seconds more.
Sift the flour with the baking powder and cinnamon and fold in with a spatula from bottom to top.
Fold the apples into the batter and pour into the tin.
Preheat the oven to 175°C; line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the tahini and icing sugar well with a spoon.
Add the flour, ground walnuts and baking powder to make a soft dough that doesn't stick to your hands; if too soft, add 1–2 spoonfuls of flour.
Take walnut-sized pieces of dough and roll into balls; place them spaced apart on the tray and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until the edges are lightly coloured.
Leave on the tray for 5 minutes; they are soft while hot and firm up as they cool.
Once completely cool, store in an airtight tin for 1 week.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; grease the ovenproof dish.
Wash the spinach in plenty of water and chop; cook in a pan for 4–5 minutes until all the liquid has evaporated.
Mix the spinach with the curd cheese and add a little salt.
Spread a little sauce in the bottom of the dish; layer the lasagne sheets, spinach filling and sauce in turn.
Finish with sauce on top; dry sheets won't cook.
Scatter the cheese and cover with foil; bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10–15 minutes more to brown.
Insert a knife: if the sheets are soft, it is ready.
Rest for 15 minutes, then slice.
Add the strained yoghurt and crushed garlic and mix until smooth.
Add the dried mint; taste before adding salt, as the cheese is salty.
Spread on a serving plate and drizzle with olive oil.
